utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in this courtroom and those just outside the courtroom assisting us. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. A few procedural issues. The Prosecution is invited to file the overview of photographs used during the testimony of Witness C-1118 so that it's clearly on the record in this table which number corresponds with which ERN number. Then we'll -- the Chamber received a form, "Absence from court due to illness," in which Mr. Stanisic has indicated that he feels unable to attend court proceedings on this date due to illness. He has not ticked the box that he has discussed the matter with counsel. Mr. Jordash, does that raise any concern?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. I think the situation is unchanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we also received a -- a form in which the UN Detention Unit Medical Service ticked some boxes as -- in relation to having examined Mr. Stanisic, that he has no observable symptoms with which the doctor can judge whether or not he's too unwell to attend court. It also says that: "Including today, I assess that he will require a zero day absence before he should be fit to attend court once more," and that the medical officer will see the detainee today. That's dated the 16th of July. The Chamber further received the -- the form in which the principal officer, Mr. Lagendijk [phoen] reports about his meeting with Mr. Stanisic today in which he announced that the court schedule was -- a court hearing was scheduled, that Mr. Stanisic indicated that he feels too unwell to attend court and at that he is not willing to wave his right to attend court in person and that he did not indicate that he wishes to use the video-conferencing link. Finally, the Chamber received the weekly medical report which says that there are no significant changes, hardly any changes compared to yesterday, apart that the mobility seems to be slightly better than it was yesterday. Any need to make further submissions or any questions for the doctor?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, could a message be sent to the doctor that we thank him had for remaining standby, and that since there are no questions for him -- perhaps you could just activate the videolink for a second. Good afternoon. Can you hear me? Can you see me? Doctor, we just went through all the paperwork, and the parties indicated to me that they have no further questions for you. The parties have no further questions for you. Therefore I would like to very much thank you for remaining standby, and you are excused.

utterances.speaker: DR. ROWELL
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We can finish the videolink. In order to use our time as efficiently as possible, the parties are requested that within half an hour of receiving the medical reports they should indicate to the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties are requested to indicate within half an hour upon having received the medical report whether there's any need for the doctor to remain standby for answering further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The only problem with that, Your Honour, is that often the Stanisic Defence are travelling to court when the report arrives. Could you also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said after receipt, which means that if you have not received it. But at the same time it might be a very practical solution that you receive a phone call perhaps once we have received it, and to the extent you want to have anything read to you, that it will be read to you by telephone and that you then make up your mind, because I find it a waste of time for the doctor to remained standby and then to hear that we have no questions for him. That's -- but of course we'll try to apply such a regime in a reasonable way, of course. And not asking from you anything in this respect, that would be unreasonable. And the Chamber is confident that it will receive your cooperation in this respect. Before we call the next witness, did we understand well, Mr. Jordash, that for the next witness there's no need to cross-examine him, at least on the basis of the statement and the transcripts?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's quite right from the Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I might say a few words about that later. Mr. Jovanovic, will you cross-examine the witness later?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. My estimate is that it will be a brief examination, maybe quarter of an hour. I will have perhaps two questions based on the previously given statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll perhaps later discuss these matters. Ms. Brehmeier, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: No protective measures, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Usher, could you please escort Ms. Denona into the courtroom. Ms. Brehmeier, will it be you who examines the witness? I saw Ms. Brehmeier nodding yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Denona. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration. The text will now be handed out by Madam Usher. I invite you to make at that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Ms. Denona.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, you'll first be examined by Ms. Brehmeier-Metz, and she is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Ms. Brehmeier.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Denona. Can you please give your full name to the court.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Jasna Denona.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: What is your maiden name?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And when and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I was born on the 22nd September 1976, in Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Do you recall giving a statement to investigators of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I would ask that 65 ter number 1163, a statement dated 2nd and 3rd of November, 2000 and -- 2000 be placed on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: On the screen before you, you see a document purporting to be a statement given by you on the 2nd and 3rd of November, 2000. Can I ask you, please, to look at the bottom of that page and at the signatures. Do you recognise any of the signatures?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Which one do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: My own.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And I then also ask you to look at the bottom of the last page of this document and tell me whether you recognise any of the signatures.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And which one do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: My signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Before you came here to The Hague to testify in this case, did you have an opportunity to review a translation of this statement in your own language?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And is there anything that you wish to change or to clarify in that statement?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I stand by the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And the statement that you signed in 2000, in November 2000, does that accurately reflect what you said to the investigators in November 2000?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions today that you were asked in 2000, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: The Prosecution moves to have 65 ter Exhibit 1163 admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P37, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, do you recall having given testimony before this Tribunal on 29th October 2003, in the case of Slobodan Milosevic, and on 9th February 2006, in the case of Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I would ask in a 65 ter number 5038, which is a copy of the transcript of this witness's testimony given before this Tribunal in the case of Slobodan Milosevic be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: After arriving here in The Hague, Ms. Denona, and in preparation for your testimony today, did you have an opportunity to review audio recordings of your testimony in the Slobodan Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And having reviewed your testimony, is there anything you wish to change or clarify?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I would then ask that 65 ter number 5039, which is a copy of the transcript of this witness's testimony in the Milan Martic case be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And again, the same question, Ms. Denona. After arriving here in The Hague and in preparation for your testimony today, did you have an opportunity to review audio recordings of your testimony in the Milan Martic case?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And having reviewed your testimony, is there anything you would wish to change or clarify?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today that you were asked in the Slobodan Milosevic case and in the Milan Martic case would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And do you affirm the truthfulness and accuracy of your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter numbers 5038 and 5039, which is the prior testimony of this witness in the Milosevic and Martic cases on 29th October 2003, and 9th February 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any objections against admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are no objections. Therefore, the transcripts of the previous testimony of the witness are admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar, would you please assign numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibits P38 and P39, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. You may proceed, Ms. Brehmeier.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would now ask 65 ter number 6 -- sorry, 2650 to be called on the screen. For Your Honours' reference, this is map 1 in the court binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, you see before you a -- an overview map of Croatia and Bosnia. This is not an official map. However, does this map give an overview of the locations of Skabrnja, Nadin, and Bruska, which is within Croatia, which is approximately correct?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I would then ask that 65 -- that map 16 of the court binder, which is ERN 0632-2720, be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar. You wanted to tender it into evidence, I took it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I intended --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't ask, but I was a bit early, Ms. Brehmeier.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I can tender it into evidence if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P40, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P40 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: The next map I would like to be shown is map 16 of the court binder, 0632-2720. And the 65 ter number, I believe, is CB-map 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, before you now is an official map. And you can see the names of the villages of Skabrnja and Nadin in red. Does this map accurately reflect the locations of Skabrnja and Nadin as being to the west of Benkovac, which is in the lower right corner of this map?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I can tender the map now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P41, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P41 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And the last map I'd like you to look at, Ms. Denona, is map 17 of the court binder, ERN 0632-2721, or 65 ter number CB-map 17. This is another official map, and you can see the name of the village of Bruska set out in red. Does this map accurately reflect the location of the village of Bruska as being to the north-east of Benkovac, which is in the -- in the lower left corner of this map.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And the Prosecution tenders this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P42, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, in your testimonies in the two cases that you appeared in previously, as well as in your statement given to investigators of the ICTY, you described the events that led to you being shot while fleeing your home on 21st December 1991. I'd like to ask you a few brief questions about this, the first one being: When someone knocked at the door on the evening of that day, who went to the front door?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I asked who was at the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And what was the response?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: The militia of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Was something else said to identify the persons outside?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes. I repeated my question. They said for the second time 'round that they were Krajina police, the so-called Martic's men.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Was the expression "Marticevci" actually used by the men?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: What did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I understood it to mean that they were the police who at that time were going under the name of Marticevci, and I presumed they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: In your testimony and statement, you then describe how you fled the house. Why did you flee?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Because before we opened the door, I had heard shots. It scared us, and we feared for our lives.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: In what direction did you flee?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: To the south, through the balcony door of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Were you followed?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Do you mean the armed people or the people who were with me in the house?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Let's start with the people who were with you in the house.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes. I fled as well as my mother and two lady neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And the armed men?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: They remained standing in front of the entrance with our neighbour Dragan, who opened the door of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Dragan after he had opened the door of the house?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Before I fled from the house, I heard a conversation. The men who came knocking asked Dragan, "Dragan, what are you doing in Bore's house?"

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And Boro being who?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Bore is my father.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Could you hear what Dragan responded to this?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Dragan told them that we were not doing anything, that we were just sitting around and talking, nothing in particular.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: When you fled, can you please describe to us what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: When you fled the house, were you shot at?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes. When I jumped the wall of the yard, one volley of fire sounded from behind me, from a distance of about 4 to 5 metres. And the next shots hit the ground near my feet, and one of the bullets hit me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Where did the bullet hit you?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: It was not only one bullet. I was hit in the hip and the right arm.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: In your opinion -- no, sorry. I rephrase the question. What did your mother wear that -- that evening?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: A skirt and a long-sleeved top.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: What did you wear?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Jeans and a T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: At that time how did you wear your hair?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Long, tied in a pig-tail.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: How was the light at that evening?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Clear, moonlight.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The hair was tied in a pony-tail.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: You then describe how you hid in the feels and later returned to the house and that you found a number of dead people there. Can you please give us the names of the people you found in the house dead?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Petar Marinovic, Svetozar Draca, Roko Marinovic, and Dusko Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And were they lying in your house or in another house?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: The next-door house belonging to Roko Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Do you know of anybody else who was killed?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Can you please give us the names.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Dragan Marinovic was killed after being hauled away from my house, and his mother, Ika Marinovic. And another four neighbours, Krste Marinovic, his wife Draginja Marinovic, another neighbour Stana Marinovic, and her sister-in-law nick-named Masa or Manda Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Was anyone wounded?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Who was wounded?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Apart from me, Ante Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: You've already told us that you were hit by two bullets. Do you know how the people you have named were killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: From firearms.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, do you recall having given a statement to the Benkovac police on 25th December 1991?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I don't remember that it was that exact date, but in the month of December, I gave a statement, sometime between the 25th and the 27th December.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I'd ask that 65 ter number 2655 be called on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: The statement that is now shown on the screen, is that the one that you gave to the police in Benkovac and that was shown to you during your testimony in the Milan Martic case?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: It's really not easily legible. The dates do not coincide. I don't think it was the 25th of December, if the left -- if the top left corner indicates the date of the giving of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: But aside from the date, do you recognise this statement?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I recognise it from seeing it in the previous case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Before you testified here today, did you have a chance to read this document in your own language?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: To the extent that it was legible, could I read it. I had the opportunity to read it, but there are -- there is certain information that is not recorded accurately.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: What is not recorded accurately?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Well, for instance, it is not verbatim what I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: What is missing in that statement?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: The thing that left the greatest impression is left out, namely that the men who burst through the door said they were Martic's men.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Other than that and taking into account that the document is very difficult to read, does this statement accurately reflect what you told the Benkovac police in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: You could say yes. You could say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? In the absence of any objections, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P42 -- 43, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P43 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, do you also recall having spoken to the Zadar police in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Could 65 ter number 5040 please be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, this is a note compiled by the Zadar police about your interview on the 13th of July, 1992. Did you have a chance to read this document in your own language before you testified here today?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Is this a true reflection of what you told the Zadar police, or is there anything you want to correct or add?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: There are points that I would correct, and there are additions I would make.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And let's deal with the corrections first. What would you like to correct?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: The incident happened at 1945 hours, not at 2015 hours. And it's not true that my mother and Dragan went into the hallway and talked to the person or persons banging on the door. It was I who talked. If -- that my mother talked to them and said that it was late and she wasn't going to open the door is not correct. They did not fire three times. It was not there that Dragan was ordered to raise his arms in the air. They asked Dragan, "What are you doing in Bore's house?" not, "What are you doing here?"

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Just let me read it to the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: You also said that there was something you wanted to add to this note. Can you tell us what you would like to add.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I thought I would add the words that I said that had been left out, but I've already said what I said then when making the corrections.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Other than the corrections you've just made, does this note accurately reflect what you said to the Zadar police on the 13th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders Exhibit number 5040 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, Madam Registrar, the number to be assigned is?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P44, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P44 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: The next exhibit I'd like you to look at, Ms. Denona, is 65 ter 1142, and I ask that that be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: This is a report by Lieutenant-Colonel Simo Rosic of the 180th Motorised Brigade of the JNA to the JNA 9th Corps, dated 11th March 1992. And at the bottom half of that page we can see that it addresses the "Massacre in Bruska."

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Can we please move to page 3 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Paragraphs three and four of that page contain information about a fight between Dusko Marinovic and Mile Pupovac three or four years prior to 1991. And they point out that this may have been the reason for the attack on the 21st of December, 1991, and that Mile Pupovac may have been one of the perpetrators. Ms. Denona, when have you first heard about a fight between Dusko Marinovic and Mile Pupovac?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I read that only in this document. I'd never heard of it otherwise in my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: The house of Dusko Marinovic, was that the only house that was attacked on the 21st of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And the people killed on the 21st of December, 1991, were they all from Dusko Marinovic's house?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Therefore, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P45, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P45 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: The last document I'd like you to look at, Ms. Denona, is 65 ter 1143. This is a note compiled by Major Branislav Ristic, also of the 180th Motorised Brigade of the JNA. It is dated 4th April 1992, and it deals with "The killings in Bruska." Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Only during proofing. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Can we please move to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Paragraph one of that page describes that the murderer or murderers of the killings in Bruska are from Medvidje, and in paragraph two it says that Pupovac and Skoric from Medvidje committed the murders in Bruska. Do you know the persons mentioned here, Pupovac and Skoric?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Other than what you have told the Court, is there anything that you would know that would identify the persons who came to your house on the 21st of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I can only say that I believe this was done by the so-called militia of Krajina, Martic's men, but based on this I can't say anything. From all I know, it was done by the people who introduced themselves when they banged on the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P46, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P46 is admitted into evidence. Ms. Brehmeier, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: And as a final issue, Ms. Denona, I'd like to briefly touch upon the wounds that you have received. You suffered a shot in your left hip and a shot in your right arm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the bullets hit your body, in the back, on one of the sides, left or right, or in the front?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: On the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Did you suffer any long-term consequences from these wounds?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes. I am disabled 50 percent. I'm registered as a civilian invalid. My arm is permanently damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Are there any long-term consequences you have suffered from the shot in your hip?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: No, nothing serious.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Would you mind showing your right arm to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Would you please show it to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness shows her right arm to the Court in which we see visible scars of what appears to be injuries. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Denona.

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Brehmeier. No cross-examination by the Stanisic Defence. Simatovic Defence, Mr. Jovanovic. Ms. Denona, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Jovanovic. Mr. Jovanovic is counsel for Mr. Simatovic. Please proceed, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Denona, I have only a few questions for you which are unrelated to the event in which you were a victim. Otherwise, I want to say that I'm sorry for the things that you went through. At the time the incident occurred, you were 15 years old; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that before the incident you were not interested in politics but, however, that you did know that Serbs had taken up certain places in the environs of your village.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes. One could know that from the news.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Denona, at the time did you know what the JNA is, what the Martic police is, irrespective of the way those people introduced themselves when they knocked on the door of your house and opened fire at you?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I could tell them apart by their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any JNA presence in your area since you say you could tell them apart because of the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Not in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean the general area around your village, not only the village itself.

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I did see them in Benkovac, Benkovac being the closest place where I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any troop movement on the part of the JNA, their vehicles, weapons?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your neighbour who was killed, Dragan, he had been mobilised into the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he receive a mobilisation call to join the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that person's full name Sveto Draca?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He wore a JNA uniform?

utterances.speaker: JASNA DENONA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Denona. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd just give us one second. Ms. Brehmeier, has the cross-examination triggered any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has no questions for you, Ms. Denona. That means that this concludes your evidence in this court. We'd like to thank you very much for coming the long way to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort Ms. Denona out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, the Chamber would invite the parties to explain to this Chamber what bringing this witness to The Hague, attending with over 30 people in this courtroom, this testimony, what it has brought us anything more than what could have achieved under Rule 92 bis? Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, exactly the questions I put to the witness, irrespective of the fact that the witness was only 15 years old at the time, which raised some doubt with me as to what formations there were at the time. She did mention mobilisation call-up papers for the person Sveto Draca from the JNA. She also mentioned some members of the Serbian paramilitary forces. What I wanted to learn from her was whether she had any realistic and factual knowledge at the time about the various uniformed personnel and units she could see in the area or whether she learned that subsequently. Since she said that she was aware of that at the time from the news, i.e., that she knew what the JNA was and what its members looked like and what weapons they had and she could differentiate between the JNA and the Martic -- Martic's Police, this is precisely what I wanted to get at, asking her whether she was familiar with any JNA presence in that area. This is relevant for our defence. I wanted to know whether in that general area there were only Serb paramilitaries whom she mentioned or those belonging to Martic's Police or whether there were any JNA soldiers there as well, and I am satisfied with the answer I received to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wasn't it at length dealt with in the cross-examination by Mr. Milosevic at the time? Not the five questions you put to her, but approximately the six, seven, eight, nine, or ten pages of cross-examination by Mr. Milosevic, asking in full detail what she knew of any military presence and activities, including JNA soldiers she saw when she went to school. Wasn't that dealt with in quite some detail, far more detailed than you asked her?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, Your Honour. However, I believe that the essence -- the crux of the cross-examination conducted by the accused Milosevic moved in the direction of the crimes being committed by those who were not members or were in anyway related to the JNA since literally this incident occurred because of some people who were out of control. Her answer in which she says that the JNA had been stationed close to JNA and that she had noticed JNA movements, it was our position that it was within the AOR of the JNA, and hence the JNA was present for that reason. As I've already said, from the cross-examination by Mr. Milosevic, one could not conclude whether the witness was at the time of the incident aware of which units, armed units, there were in the area or whether she learned about that after having been wounded. As she shared with us, she said that she could learn from the news who was present in that area at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The same question for you, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The simple answer, Your Honour, from our perspective is we have no instructions. And so decisions which we would be able to make much earlier if we had instructions cannot -- sometimes cannot be made at all. In this instance, we made the decision not to cross-examine. Not on the basis of instructions but on the basis of what we perceived to be the best interests of our client. That decision could only be made quite late in the day after considerable thought and considerable cross-referencing of various materials and, even then, with some reluctance given that we are in this difficult ethical position of acting without instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because you earlier may have had on your mind that you wanted to cross-examine the witness, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And without instructions you changed your mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So at the time you had reason to prepare for cross-examination, whereas now, without any further instructions you refrain from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis that we are trying to gauge what is a sensible course to travel to, on the one hand, provide our client with a reasonable and forthright defence; and on the other hand, to remain as close as we can to our ethical commitment under the code of conduct to act on instructions, an almost impossible balancing exercise given the code of conduct and given our lack of instructions, but we're doing the best we can to assist our client and assist the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the time when you said you wanted to cross-examine the witness, did you have any instructions at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. I mean, our fallback position in that situation is first to assume we do have cross-examination if anything appears to arise from the statement, and then to slowly move towards a position whereby we can accept as much as we think is safe to accept in light of the considerations I've just outlined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Ms. Brehmeier, have you considered to speak with the Defence about the necessity of calling this witness as a viva voce witness rather than to re-seek this witness to be called as a 92 bis witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the fact that any 92 bis motion of the Prosecution since 2007 has been entirely opposed by the Defence, I did not see much use in addressing this specific issue with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties will understand why I put these questions after consultation with my colleagues, because what we have now is -- let me ask you one further question. Is there any dispute about the presence of JNA forces on the 21st of December, 1991, in the Benkovac area?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: That is difficult for me to answer, Your Honour, because certainly with the Simatovic Defence we have not been able to reach any agreement on any facts based, for example, on the Martic judgement, so I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you if the Simatovic Defence would take the position that JNA forces were present in the Benkovac area, I'm not asking about what they were doing there but whether troops were there and may have moved around, would that be a point the Prosecution would dispute?

utterances.speaker: MS. BREHMEIER-METZ
utterances.text: I wouldn't think so, but I haven't heard anything from the Simatovic Defence in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but apparently the whole purpose of the cross-examination has been to -- to establish that there was JNA presence and movement, unless there's anything else, Mr. Jovanovic, which I may have missed. Because I jotted down how old she was at the time; well, that's not entirely new in this testimony. Whether she knew about JNA; we see already in the statement that she's talking about green olive JNA uniforms; and apparently there's no dispute about whether there was any JNA presence of troops in the area, and that was specified in the Benkovac area. The -- then finally the only thing that remained was whether Dragan or, later, Sveto was mobilised, and that is dealt with in the statement as well if I am not mistaken, Mr. Jovanovic. Or is there anything entirely knew of substance which you learned today from this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, I must say that Defence accepted many adjudicated facts, and the Prosecution is aware of that, hence their argument is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, I asked you a question. I didn't invite you to respond to what Mrs. Brehmeier has said. I asked you what is new and of substance you learned which is not yet contained in the witness statement, what is not yet contained in the two transcripts, and matters of substance I would consider matters where you could reasonably expect that they would be in dispute. And we just learned that the JNA presence in the Benkovac area on the 21st of December, 1991, is not disputed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the first page of the statement the witness mentioned members of the Serb paramilitaries, paramilitary forces. Then she mentioned that Sveto Draca had been mobilised into the JNA. At the end, describing the incident in which she was wounded, she mentioned Martic's Police. Having in mind that she was 15 years of age at the time, I was doubtful as to whether at the time she could distinguish between those units that were present so as to be able to characterise one unit as a paramilitary unit; another unit as a JNA unit; and thirdly, Martic's Police. That is why I asked the witness whether being 15 years old at the time she knew who they were and who was or was not present in that area. Irrespective of her age at the time of the incident, she told us that she learned from the news of the units and that she could identify the JNA as such. I believe that that piece of information -- or, rather, that that conclusion could not be arrived at from the statement itself as well as on the basis of the testimony in the Milosevic case. I was interested in whether she knew about who the people involved were then or whether she learned of that later given the fact that nine years have elapsed. Since she said that she could recognise JNA uniforms, at the time, I put the follow-up question as to whether she knew of any JNA presence, movement, and weapons in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apparently this is not in dispute, so whether there's any need to ask whether at that time a 15-year-old witness was able to establish this, and then of course what one would have expected where she describes in her statement and her testimony what she saw when she went to school, et cetera, and she describes the colours of the uniforms, what now is added by asking, "Were you able to see whether these were JNA?" An apparently undisputed fact. And of course I'm not saying that if there's a good reason to call a witness for cross-examination that you should not ask that question, but again there's no dispute about it. And what we see is we have asked a young woman to travel for 2.000 kilometres to come here and to go back, to give a statement or to testify where we have had one statement, two transcripts of testimony where nothing of substance is added. And to the extent anything is added, it is a matter which is not in dispute, and that kept us, well over 30 people, busy over the last one hour and a half. We all had to prepare. We all had to be here. This Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I've verified with my colleagues, just a waste of time. And the Chamber expects the parties to communicate in such a way and to consider what are the core issues in this case, so as this to never happen again. We stand adjourned until the 20th of July, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of July, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.37 p.m.,
